answers.solution:
I investigated the environment, cloned the project (`/workspace/chimera-v2`), reproduced the bug, analyzed it, and verified the fix. The deliverable is written to `/workspace/SOLUTION.md`.

Key findings:

**Root cause** — In `src/chimera/gateway.py`, `resolve_litellm_model()` had branches only for LiteLLM-native providers (`zai`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `google`, `deepseek`, `openai`). A config-only provider like `hermes` fell through returning the raw catalog id with no `api_base`/`custom_llm_provider`, so LiteLLM raised `BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided`. Grep confirmed `providers.<name>.base_url` was read *only* by `config._is_local_base_url()` (a keyless-loopback probe), and `complete()` passed neither the provider `base_url` nor its resolved `api_key`.

**Fix** (2 hunks, placed after every native branch / the `litellm_model` early return):
1. Add optional `base_url` to `resolve_litellm_model`, plus a generic branch returning `("openai/" + model_name.rsplit("/",1)[-1], {api_base: base_url, custom_llm_provider: "openai"})`.
2. In `LiteLLMGateway.complete()`, look up `self.config.providers[effective_provider]`, pass its `base_url`, and fall back to `provider_cfg.api_key` when `api_keys` has no entry (so `api_key_env`-resolved credentials authenticate).

**Verification (actually run):**
- RED against pre-fix `gateway.py`: `16 failed, 7 passed` — matches the expected signature.
- GREEN against fixed code: `23 passed`.
- The end-to-end test drives a real `litellm.acompletion` at a stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` stub on loopback and asserts the stub saw bare model `glm-5.3-flash` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- `ruff check`: clean.

Full write-up with the exact diff, reproduction script, and commands is in `/workspace/SOLUTION.md`.

signatures.description: Symptom: adding an OpenAI-compatible provider to chimera.yaml purely by config (providers.<name>.base_url + api_key_env + a catalog model) fails at call time with litellm BadRequestError 'LLM Provider NOT provided. Pass in the LLM provider you are trying to call. You passed model=hermes/glm-5.3-flash'. Root cause: gateway.resolve_litellm_model handled only providers with a LiteLLM-native prefix (zai/deepseek hardcode api_base + custom_llm_provider; openrouter/anthropic/google/openai get a prefix) and fell through otherwise returning the catalog id with NO api_base, so config.providers[name].base_url never reached the LLM call - the config-only custom-endpoint path was dead despite the config schema advertising it. Diagnosis steps: (1) grep every read of providers[].base_url in the package - the only hit was _is_local_base_url, i.e. the base_url was used for a keyless-loopback check and nowhere else; (2) confirm the call site (LiteLLMGateway.complete) passes only api_key from config.api_keys, never the provider base_url; (3) reproduce with a real call, not a mock. Fix shape: add an optional base_url parameter threaded from complete() (which holds the config), and a generic branch mirroring the zai branch - return ('openai/' + bare model id after the last '/', {api_base: base_url, custom_llm_provider: 'openai'}), placed AFTER every native branch and after the explicit litellm_model early return so nothing native changes; also fall back to providers.<name>.api_key (what api_key_env resolves to at load time) when api_keys has no shortcut entry, since a generic provider authenticates only through that key. Prove it hermetically: a stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer stub on 127.0.0.1 driven by a real litellm.acompletion asserting the stub saw the bare model id and the Bearer header, plus a RED run of the same tests against the pre-fix gateway.py (observed 16 failed / 7 passed). Lesson: a config schema that advertises a field is not evidence the field is read; grep the field's read sites before calling a feature config-only.
